engineering_letters.title: Engineering Report Prepared for Barrette Outdoor Living - Calculations for Full and Half Privacy Railing with Plated Posts-ScrewBoss (IBC 2018 and IRC 2018)
engineering_letters.product_evaluated: Aluminum-post 'plated posts / ScrewBoss' privacy railing/fence system (6005-T5 aluminum posts, rails and mounting plates; PVC infill slats, Fty = 6.2 ksi; also references Barrette 'DSP' polypropylene decorative screen panel infill tested to IBC 2018 1607.8.1.2)
engineering_letters.applicability_caveat: IMPORTANT: This is Barrette Outdoor Living's (Freedom's parent company) publicly hosted PE-stamped report, but its stated scope is a GUARDRAIL/RAILING product (explicitly validated against IRC 2018 36in and IBC 2018 42in guardrail height requirements, aluminum posts, 'privacy railing' terminology) with a mixed-material aluminum-frame + PVC/DSP-infill construction. This matches Barrette/Freedom's 'Alloy Mixed Material' fencing infill system far more closely than it matches Freedom's all-vinyl (PVC post/rail) product lines such as Emblem, Wakefield, Conway, Freeport, or Shadowbox. It is included here as the only publicly downloadable PE-stamped structural document found for the Barrette/Freedom fence family, and its Section V 'WIND DESIGN FOR SOLID FENCES' calculation (ASCE 7-16 Ch. 29.3/29.4 methodology, Kz/Kd/Kzt/G/Cf terms) demonstrates the wind-load methodology Barrette applies to solid privacy panels generally. Do NOT treat the post-spacing table below as certified for pure-PVC Freedom panel lines without separate verification - no equivalent all-vinyl-post engineering letter was found in public search.

key_content.conclusion: Resisting moment exceeds flexure moments for evaluated configurations; half-privacy and full-privacy panels require added intermediate posts for certain panel widths at higher wind speeds/exposures per the post-spacing table.

wind_load_tables.source: Barrette Outdoor Living Engineering Report (Privacy-Railing-2021-report-PE.pdf), pp.20-23 of 18
wind_load_tables.source_caveat: Same applicability caveat as engineering_letters entry above - product tested is the mixed-material aluminum-post/PVC-infill railing system, not confirmed identical to Freedom's all-PVC panel lines. Reproduced verbatim; not extrapolated or recalculated.
wind_load_tables.table_type: Recommended post spacing (on-center) by panel height, wind speed, and ASCE 7-16 exposure category
wind_load_tables.governing_load_note: '50plf on top rail' rows are governed by the 50 lb/ft top-rail point/distributed load requirement (non-wind-governed), not wind pressure; all other rows are wind-pressure-governed (psf).
footnotes: 6FT is nominal size of the panel, which is 68in
3FT (and similar fractional spacings) is a distance measured from center of the line post to the center of an added intermediate post
Suggestion to use #8 screw to secure slats in the 6FT wide spans

wind_load_tables.source: Freedom Vinyl Fencing Special Order Catalog 2024 (2024-Freedom-VF-Catalog-01-24_SpecialOrderCatalog.pdf), 'Wind Code Overview', p.10 of 112
wind_load_tables.table_type: Prescriptive wind-code hardware requirement (not a load-vs-spacing engineering table; no psf/mph values given)
wind_load_tables.content: Ready-to-Assemble fence styles require post inserts in most post configurations (not needed in corner posts) to pass wind code regulations. 8' Emblem and 6' Everton panels also require rail insert kits inserted into the top and bottom rails for additional strength in high-wind areas. Pre-Assembled fence styles require installation with the Freedom 2-pack Aluminum Bracket Kit AND post inserts in every post to pass wind code regulations.
wind_load_tables.note: This is a prescriptive compliance instruction, not an engineered psf/mph table. No numeric wind-speed or exposure-category design values are given in this catalog section.

structural_reinforcement_supplement.note: Consolidated post-insert / rail-insert / bracket reinforcement spec table from the 2024 Freedom Vinyl Fencing Special Order Catalog 'Wind Code Overview' (p.10) and 'Accessories' sections. This directly addresses the pass-1 gap where post reinforcement was only known via third-party Barrette category references.
structural_reinforcement_supplement.compliance_rule: Ready-to-Assemble fence styles require post inserts in most post configurations (not needed in corner posts) to pass wind code regulations. 8ft Emblem and 6ft Everton panels additionally require rail insert kits in the top and bottom rails for extra strength in high-wind areas. Pre-Assembled fence styles require BOTH the Freedom 2-pack Aluminum Bracket Kit AND post inserts in every post to pass wind code regulations.
structural_reinforcement_supplement.post_insert_material: Metal (aluminum, per third-party install-video description of the Estateline/Barrette-family 'metal insert' - catalog itself does not explicitly print the alloy; sold as 'Aluminum Bracket Kit' for the separate bracket hardware, which IS explicitly labeled aluminum). Not confirmed steel vs aluminum for every insert SKU from the catalog text alone - see caveat below.
structural_reinforcement_supplement.post_insert_material_caveat: The 2024 catalog text does not explicitly state the metal alloy of the post inserts themselves (it only explicitly calls the separate 2-pack bracket 'Aluminum Bracket Kit'). Pass-1 data already carries 'Aluminum (on 3 sides, per third-party retail listings)' for the 5x5 gate post insert - this pass did not find a manufacturer document that states the post-insert alloy more precisely than that. Flagging as still not fully disclosed rather than guessing.

cad_structural_detail_drawings.notes: No publicly downloadable CAD section-detail drawings, footing-detail drawings, or DWG/DXF files were located for Freedom/Barrette vinyl fencing in this pass. The closest available structural graphics are: (1) the scanned Miami-Dade NOA PDFs (24-0117.05 / 22-0217.05), which per Miami-Dade's product-control convention typically embed an approved 'Drawing No. 001' installation/section detail inside the NOA package itself (not separately extractable as text since these are scanned/image PDFs - would require visual/OCR review of the downloaded PDF pages to confirm), and (2) the PE engineering report's embedded rail/post cross-section diagrams (page 5-13 of the Privacy-Railing-2021-report-PE.pdf), which are raster images within the PDF showing section geometry for TOP RAIL EPN-0559, MID RAIL EPN-0670, END POST EPN-0667, LINE POST EPN-0669 with dimensioned Ix/Iy/section modulus - these are engineering section properties, not full CAD installation drawings.
